arxiv-2101-00053.title: A note on combining chaotic dynamical systems using the fuzzy logic XOR operator.
arxiv-2101-00053.creator: Rezki Chemlal, Laboratoire de Mathématiques Appliquées, Faculté des sciences exactes.Université Abderahmane Mira Bejaia.06000 Bejaia Algeria
arxiv-2101-00053.description: Abstract In this paper we explore whatever combining two chaotic dynamical systems using the fuzzy logic operator XOR can maintain or not the chaotic properties of the resulting dynamical system. This study is motivated by techniques used in applications to secure communications ,images encryption and cryptography. Key words : Chaos, fuzzy logic, ergodic theory, full branch.

arxiv-2108-03408.title: Enhanced nonlinear quantum metrology with weakly coupled solitons and particle losses Preprint: APS/123-QED
arxiv-2108-03408.creator: Alexander Alodjants, Dmitriy Tsarev, The Vinh Ngo, Ray-Kuang Lee
arxiv-2108-03408.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Alexander Alodjants, Dmitriy Tsarev, The Vinh Ngo, Ray-Kuang Lee. The estimation of physical parameters with Heisenberg sensitivity and beyond is one of the crucial problems for current quantum metrology. However, unavoidable lossy effect is commonly believed to be the main obstacle when applying fragile quantum states.

arxiv-2303-04400.title: Think Physics, Think Man: Barriers to Women’s Participation in Physics Education (OPINION)
arxiv-2303-04400.creator: Eliot Walton
arxiv-2303-04400.description: Abstract 1 Framework This text focuses on women because the research that is available tends to fall into binary gender categories. This work is not generalisable to other genders without further research. Furthermore, while the discussion draws on my experience as a trans-woman, I have omitted a discussion of trans-specific issues (such as transition leave and transphobia) for generality.

arxiv-2404-08718.title: Evaluation of multi-parameter likelihoods through iteration of two-dimensional slices
arxiv-2404-08718.creator: Joel S. Jayson
arxiv-2404-08718.description: Abstract In this paper we introduce a method for resolving multi-parameter likelihoods by fixing all parameter values, but two. Evaluation of those two variables is followed by iteratively cycling through each of the parameters in turn until convergence. We test the technique on the temperature power spectrum of the lensed cosmic microwave background (CMB).

arxiv-2405-12918.title: Impact of inhomogeneous diffusion on secondary cosmic ray and antiproton local spectra
arxiv-2405-12918.creator: Miguel A. Sánchez-Conde
arxiv-2405-12918.description: Abstract Recent γ \gamma -ray and neutrino observations seem to favor the consideration of non-uniform diffusion of cosmic rays (CRs) throughout the Galaxy. In this study, we investigate the consequences of spatially-dependent inhomogeneous propagation of CRs on the fluxes of secondary CRs and antiprotons detected at Earth.

arxiv-2506-05831.title: Heartcare Suite: Multi-dimensional Understanding of ECG with Raw Multi-lead Signal Modeling
arxiv-2506-05831.creator: Yihan Xie 1,* , Sijing Li 1,* , Tianwei Lin 1,* , Zhuonan Wang 1,* , Chenglin Yang 1 , Yu Zhong 1 , Wenqiao Zhang 1 , Haoyuan Li 2 , Hao Jiang 2 , Fengda Zhang 1 , Qishan Chen 3 , Jun Xiao 1 , Yueting Zhuang 1 , Beng Chin Ooi 4 1 Zhejiang University, 2 Alibaba, 3 Xinhua Hospital of Shanghai Jiaotong
arxiv-2506-05831.description: Abstract We present Heartcare Suite , a multimodal comprehensive framework for fine-grained electrocardiogram (ECG) understanding. It comprises three key components: (i) Heartcare-220K , a high-quality, structured, and comprehensive multimodal ECG dataset covering essential tasks such as disease diagnosis, waveform morphology analysis, and rhythm interpretation.

arxiv-2507-05931.title: Exploring Gain-Doped-Waveguide-Synapse for Neuromorphic Applications: A Pulsed Pump-Signal Approach
arxiv-2507-05931.creator: R. Otupiri, R. Stabile
arxiv-2507-05931.description: Abstract Neuromorphic computing promises to transform AI systems by enabling them to perceive, respond to, and adapt swiftly and accurately to dynamic data and user interactions. However, traditional silicon-based and hybrid electronic technologies for artificial neurons constrain neuromorphic processors in terms of flexibility, scalability, and energy efficiency.

arxiv-2508-12734.title: Critical fluctuations of last passage percolation with thick boundaries
arxiv-2508-12734.creator: Elnur Emrah, Patrik L. Ferrari, Min Liu
arxiv-2508-12734.description: Abstract We consider the exponential last passage percolation (LPP) with thick two-sided boundary that consists of a few inhomogeneous columns and rows. Ben Arous and Corwin previously studied the limit fluctuations in this model except in a critical regime, for which they predicted that the limit distribution exists and depends only on the most dominant columns and rows.

pmc-10719393.title: Accessing gold p-acid reactivity under electrochemical anode oxidation (EAO) through oxidation relay
pmc-10719393.creator: Shuyao Zhang, Jingwen Wei, Xiaohan Ye, Angel Perez, Xiaodong Shi
pmc-10719393.description: The gold π-acid activation under electrochemical conditions is achieved. While EAO allows easy access to gold(III) intermediates over alternative chemical oxidation under mild conditions, the reported examples so far are limited to coupling reactions due to the rapid AuIII reductive elimination. Using aryl hydrazine-HOTf salt as precursors, the π-activation reaction mode was realized through oxidation relay.

pmc-11331008.title: Early onset of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) following postpartum eclampsia—A case report
pmc-11331008.creator: Kaleem ullah, Hussain Haider Shah, Maryam Tariq, Malik Olatunde Oduoye
pmc-11331008.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Key Clinical MessageEarly screening and management of postpartum posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) can reduce hospital stay and complications. Obstetricians, gynecologists, ophthalmologists, and even general physicians should be aware of PRES since its presentation is variable.Keywords: posterior leukoencephalopathy syndrome, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, postpartum period, PRES, reversible posterior leukoencephalopathy syndrome INTRODUCTION After 20 weeks of pregnancy, gestational hypertension is common and can lead to life‐threatening complications for some women.

pmc-11486902.title: Substrate engagement by the intramembrane metalloprotease SpoIVFB
pmc-11486902.creator: Melanie A Orlando, Hunter J T Pouillon, Saikat Mandal, Lee Kroos, Benjamin J Orlando
pmc-11486902.description: S2P intramembrane metalloproteases regulate diverse signaling pathways across all three domains of life. However, the mechanism by which S2P metalloproteases engage substrates and catalyze peptide hydrolysis within lipid membranes has remained elusive. Here we determine the cryo-EM structure of the S2P family intramembrane metalloprotease SpoIVFB from Bacillus subtilis bound to its native substrate Pro-σK.

pmc-11572072.title: Implementing geriatric assessment for dose optimization of CDK4/6 inhibitors in older breast cancer patients
pmc-11572072.creator: Antonis Valachis, Laura Biganzoli, Athina Christopoulou, Kamilla Fjermeros, Elena Fountzila, Jürgen Geisler, Raquel Gomez-Bravo, Peeter Karihtala, Paris Kosmidis, Angelos Koutras, Helena Linardou, Henrik Lindman, Iván Martínez-Ballestero, Anna Belén Rodríguez, Icro Meattini, Montserrat Munoz-Mateu,
pmc-11572072.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Current evidence from both randomized trials and real-world studies suggests that older patients with advanced hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative (HR+/HER2) breast cancer derive clinical benefit from the addition of CDK4/6 inhibitors to endocrine therapy. However, a higher risk for adverse events due to CDK4/6 inhibitors among older patients is evident, leading to a trend of initiating CDK4/6 inhibitors at lower dose in clinical practice, though without evidence.

pmc-11596809.title: Use of Epinephrine in Cardiac Arrest: Advances and Future Challenges
pmc-11596809.creator: Caitlin A Williams, Hannah E Fairley, Quincy K Tran, Ali Pourmand, Gregor Prosen
pmc-11596809.description: Epinephrine is the most common medication used in cardiac arrest. Although the medication has been a mainstay of treatment over the last century, the utility and efficacy of epinephrine has been re-evaluated in recent years. This study aims to evaluate the literature describing the efficacy, timing, and dosing of epinephrine use in cardiac arrest.

pmc-11624742.title: Is flat rate pricing for unlimited alcohol consumption associated with problematic alcohol consumption patterns? A cross-sectional study with the Japan COVID-19 and Society Internet Survey
pmc-11624742.creator: Mami Wakabayashi, Aya Kinjo, Yoshifumi Sugiyama, Midori Takada, Hiroyasu Iso, Takahiro Tabuchi
pmc-11624742.description: AbstractObjectivesThis study investigates the relationship between flat rate pricing for unlimited alcohol consumption in restaurants and bar and problematic alcohol consumption patterns identified by the Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test (AUDIT) during the COVID-19 pandemic.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted using data from the Japan Society and New Tobacco Internet Survey in February 2022.

pmc-12434849.title: Contraceptive care and method use by sexual and gender minority status: insights from a longitudinal panel of sexual and reproductive healthcare patients in Wisconsin
pmc-12434849.creator: Ellie Leong, Christina E. Geddes, Fiona Weeks, Megan L. Kavanaugh
pmc-12434849.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Access to sexual and reproductive health (SRH) care is key for people to realise their reproductive goals, but sexual and gender minority (SGM) patients may experience different barriers or facilitators to access than their non-SGM counterparts. We analysed a panel dataset of 900 patients using publicly funded SRH services in Wisconsin in 2020–2023 and constructed conditional logistic regression models to explore barriers to contraceptive services and subsequent patient-centred contraceptive method use, stratified by SGM status.

pmc-12547112.title: Early cancer detection: Analysis of a comprehensive screening program in a private clinic in Peru
pmc-12547112.creator: Alejandro Leon Garrido-Lecca, Roberto E Alvarado-Cordova, Carlos Carracedo, Virgilio E Failoc-Rojas
pmc-12547112.description: Background:Early cancer detection is crucial for improving patient prognosis and survival. However, in Latin America, the implementation of screening programs faces economic and logistical barriers.Design and methods:This study evaluates the utility of an early detection program in a private clinic in Peru. A prospective study was conducted at the clinic’s Oncology Center between 2017 and 2019.

pmc-12735924.title: Targeting Human Cytomegalovirus as a Novel Approach for Glioblastoma Treatment
pmc-12735924.creator: Thelma Flores, Eloïse Delpierre, Ghislain Male, Claire Gourin, Sébastien Hantz, Alexia Damour, Gaëtan Ligat, Yuying Liang
pmc-12735924.description: Glioblastoma (GB) is a highly aggressive brain tumor with a very poor prognosis. Treatment usually consists of surgery, followed by radiotherapy and chemotherapy, but the prognosis remains poor due to its resistance to therapies and a high recurrence rate. Multiple studies have reported the presence of human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) proteins and/or nucleic acids in GB tissues, suggesting its possible implication.

pmc-13258079.title: Multisensory virtual reality reduces postoperative delirium in elderly patients undergoing laparoscopic gastrointestinal surgery
pmc-13258079.creator: Wenjun Luo, Yi Duan, Tingting Ni, Zhuqun Mao, Zhifeng Gao
pmc-13258079.description: BACKGROUNDEffective interventions for postoperative delirium (POD) remain unclear. Research indicates that light and sound stimulation may enhance the functional connectivity of the medial visual network, while olfactory stimulation improves cognitive function. This study aims to address POD by integrating auditory, olfactory and visual stimuli to develop a multisensory virtual reality device.

pmc-13329065.title: Impending crisis in oral and maxillofacial surgery in Korea related to the government’s structural transformation project for tertiary general hospitals
pmc-13329065.creator: Tae-Geon Kwon
pmc-13329065.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ented the “Support Project for the Structural Transformation of Tertiary General Hospitals” (hereafter referred to as the Structural Transformation Project). The primary objective of this initiative is to restore the original role of tertiary hospitals by encouraging them to focus on severe, emergency, and rare diseases while reducing the treatment of relatively mild conditions that can be managed at primary or secondary healthcare institutions.

pmc-13406892.title: Biomarkers for Necrotising Enterocolitis—Are We There Yet?
pmc-13406892.creator: Anna Jackson, Maria Cifuentes Nino, Janet Berrington
pmc-13406892.description: Necrotising enterocolitis (NEC) remains an important disease for neonatologists, with diagnostic and management challenges and impacts on mortality and neurodisability. NEC can present in a non-specific way, and differentiating from late-onset sepsis (LOS), focal perforation (FIP) and feed intolerance can be difficult. Biomarkers have been extensively explored as a way to help more definitively identify NEC or rule it out.

pmc-13424456.title: Cerebral differences between roller and speed skaters: preliminary evidence for roller-to-ice talent transfer
pmc-13424456.creator: Qing Yan, Keying Zhang, Ling Jiang, Yuyan Wang, Yihua Cao, Chunmei Cao, Dong Zhang
pmc-13424456.description: ObjectivesTalent transfer (TT) from roller skating to speed skating is a recognized pathway for developing elite athletes. This study aimed to identify the sport-specific cerebral characteristics in these athletes by comparing their brain structure and function, thereby providing preliminary neuroimaging evidence relevant to “roller-to-ice” TT.
